outcomeNote: A further aggadic dictum of R' Elazar (ואמר), one of a series of his statements begun in the preceding units; no dialectic.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִיּוֹם שֶׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ נִפְסְקָה חוֹמַת בַּרְזֶל בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאַתָּה קַח לְךָ מַחֲבַת בַּרְזֶל וְנָתַתָּ אוֹתָהּ קִיר בַּרְזֶל בֵּינְךָ וּבֵין הָעִיר״.
segments.en: «And Rabbi Elazar said: Since the day the Temple was destroyed an iron wall separates Israel from their Father in heaven, as it is stated» to the prophet Ezekiel, instructing him to symbolize that separation: «“And take for yourself an iron griddle, and set it as an iron wall between yourself and the city…»it will be a sign for the house of Israel” (Ezekiel 4:3).
